title: A Randomized Trial of Standard vs. Hypofractionated Accelerated Radiotherapy for Progression in Limited-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
official: A Randomized Trial of Standard vs. Hypofractionated Accelerated Radiotherapy for Progression in Limited-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer (SHARP-SCLC)
summary: This study aims to determine whether an abbreviated course of thoracic radiotherapy, delivered in five fractions over one week between chemotherapy cycles, improves progression-free survival compared with standard radiotherapy delivered concurrently with chemotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* New diagnosis of Limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), eligible for curative intent concurrent chemoradiotherapy

  \-- Planned for immunotherapy and prophylactic cranial irradiation is allowed and encouraged
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0-2
* Age 18 years or older
* Life expectancy \> 3 months
* Willingness and ability to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior thoracic radiation therapy (RT) which, in the opinion of the treating radiation oncologist, precludes the delivery of further thoracic RT

  * If there has been prior thoracic RT, a composite of all RT plans must be created, and the dose constraints herein must still be met
  * An allowance for 10% repair is permitted if at least 12 months have passed between the prior RT and the trial protocol specified RT
* Serious medical comorbidities which, in the opinion of the treating radiation oncologist, preclude the delivery of RT

  \-- This includes interstitial lung disease
* Patients who have started systemic treatment for LS-SCLC but are unable to start radiation with cycle 3 or earlier (delaying scheduled chemotherapy without clinical indication) is not permitted
* Pregnant or lactating women
* Inability to attend the full course of RT or planed follow-up visits
sponsor: London Health Sciences Centre Research Institute OR Lawson Research Institute of St. Joseph's
